svg.title: Difference-polynomial identity bridge
svg.desc: A changed degree-one teaching case turns two agreement inputs into zeros of h=f-g, then compares that with the nonzero degree-one zero bound. It is not the supplied Q8 instance.

g.text: f(a)=g(a) and f(b)=g(b), with a ≠ b
Must f and g match everywhere?
Define h(x)=f(x)-g(x). Then h(a)=0 and h(b)=0.
If h were nonzero and deg h ≤ 1:
nonzero degree ≤ 1 → at most one distinct zero
Remaining branch: h is identically zero. Interpret what that says about f and g.
